title: Console walkthrough - usage analytics & cost breakdown - Marlin Health
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Marlin Health through the Redwood Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Discussion focused on per-route cost attribution, token-level spend, deduping/ caching effects, dedicated vs hosted for cost predictability, and security/compliance (SOC2, KMS). Agreed next steps: send tailored pricing sheet, share SOC2 & network diagram, schedule pilot benchmark with 1-week test data.
action_items: Aisha Patel: send customized pricing + example per-route cost spreadsheet (due 2026-08-06)
Liam Chen: share runbook for pilot benchmarking and expected metrics (due 2026-08-07)
Marcus Blythe (Marlin): provide representative traffic pattern and sample prompts (due 2026-08-05)
Sofia Ruiz: schedule pilot kickoff meeting (due 2026-08-10)
next_steps: AE to email pricing and per-route cost model
SE to run pilot benchmark on hosted small scale then Dedicated suggestion
Marlin to send traffic sample and security contact for SOC2 review
transcript: 14:00:01 - Aisha Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Aisha from Redwood. quick intro, Liam our SE will do most of the console walk. 14:00:10 - Dana Ortiz: Hi all, thanks. We're excited to see the usage analytics, hoping to understand per-feature cost. 14:00:22 - Liam Chen: Great, so first page is the Console home, we show token-level spend, per-route breakdowns, and latencies. you'll see a heatmap of top routes by cost and p95 latency. 14:01:05 - Marcus Blythe: when you say per-route cost, is that down to the prompt and response tokens or do you include warm-up / cache misses? 14:01:18 - Liam Chen: good q. cost is broken into prompt tokens, completion tokens, and infrastructure overhead; we show cache hits vs misses where KV cache applies. note that automatic prefix caching can lower billed tokens for repeated prompts. 14:02:00 - Sofia Ruiz: (screen share) I'm opening the Route dashboard for "patient-summary" route - this is a common pattern we see for healthcare customers: short prompts, long completions. 14:02:30 - Dana Ortiz: our summaries are long and generate high completion token counts, worried about monthly spend. 14:02:45 - Liam Chen: understood. in the dashboard you can filter by model variant, quantization profile, and route. we also show a simulated cost if you switch to a quantized variant or enable batching - the console surfaces expected token savings. 14:03:30 - Tom Reynolds: can you show the cost breakdown by model and by route so finance can justify? 14:03:45 - Aisha Patel: yes the cost export gives per-route daily cost, model used, and latency. many customers send that to finance, it's CSV/BI friendly. 14:04:10 - Liam Chen: jumping to the Cost Explorer, you'll notice we annotate spikes with sample requests; sometimes spikes are due to a partner sending bulk backfills. 14:04:45 - Marcus Blythe: I saw a note about dedicated capacity. does Dedicated lower unit cost? what's the tradeoff vs Hosted? 14:05:05 - Liam Chen: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and better per-token economics at scale because of reserved GPU pricing and optimized batching. Hosted is simplest to get started - we offer autoscaling and burst. tradeoffs: dedicated requires commit and different networking (VPC options) but gives SLA-backed latency. 14:05:40 - Dana Ortiz: from a security perspective, we need SOC 2, SSO, and KMS integration. any pitfalls? 14:05:55 - Sofia Ruiz: we support SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning, per-route RBAC in the Console, and KMS integrations for Private deployments. we'll share SOC2 report and a network diagram. sometimes transcription: "KMS" came out in the notes as "K M S". 14:06:30 - Liam Chen: small note on caching: if your workflow is many short queries with overlapping contexts, enabling prefix/KV cache can reduce the model token count significantly, but you need to think about cache invalidation for PHI-sensitive data. 14:07:05 - Marcus Blythe: so cache is OK with PHI if we use encryption and retention policies? 14:07:20 - Sofia Ruiz: yes, with Private or Dedicated you can configure KMS and retention TTLs, and we can disable caching on sensitive routes. 14:07:50 - Tom Reynolds: curious about attribution - if multiple products call the same model, can we attribute cost per product or per team? 14:08:05 - Liam Chen: the per-route dashboard is how we recommend doing that - you can tag routes with product/team and we aggregate costs. CSV export supports tags. 14:08:30 - Dana Ortiz: how accurate are the "simulated" savings when you toggle quantization? 14:08:45 - Liam Chen: they are estimates derived from benchmark profiles for each model/quantization combo - accuracy is usually within 5-12% depending on your prompt distribution. for production we recommend a short pilot. 14:09:20 - Aisha Patel: we also have Redwood Optimize which suggests batching configs, quantization profiles, and cache rules based on your actual traffic. it can auto-suggest per-route settings. 14:09:42 - Marcus Blythe: is Optimize an extra cost? 14:09:50 - Aisha Patel: Optimize is an add-on, pricing depends on throughput and retention; we can include that in the pricing sheet. 14:10:15 - Dana Ortiz: ok show me a real example of a route with batching turned on. 14:10:30 - Sofia Ruiz: (screen) here's "claim-extract" route; you can see before/after: requests/sec, average tokens, and effective cost per thousand requests. batching increased throughput and lowered per-request cost but added about 40ms tail latency - we show a latency SLO overlay so you can decide. 14:11:12 - Tom Reynolds: can you set per-route latency targets and fallback policies? 14:11:25 - Liam Chen: yes you can set SLOs and automatic fallback to smaller models or Hosted fallback if Dedicated capacity is constrained. policies are in the Rollouts tab. 14:12:00 - Marcus Blythe: for the pilot, can we run a benchmark that mirrors our traffic and compare hosted vs dedicated? 14:12:12 - Liam Chen: absolutely. typical approach: 1) you give us a week of de-identified traffic or synthetic distribution, 2) we run a hosted baseline, 3) run a Dedicated-config simulation (or short Dedicated run if you want real numbers) and provide a cost/latency comparison. 14:12:45 - Dana Ortiz: what's the SLA for Dedicated? 14:12:55 - Aisha Patel: Dedicated has an SLA for uptime and p95 latency targets based on the committed instance size - we can include the SLA doc. 14:13:10 - Marcus Blythe: any limits on model variants - we use some fine-tuned models internally. 14:13:20 - Sofia Ruiz: you can bring custom models for Private or Dedicated; for Hosted we have an onboarding flow. fine-tuned weights may need compatibility checks with our runtime (kv cache and quantization), we'll help with that. 14:14:00 - Tom Reynolds: security paperwork - we will want SOC2, data flow, and maybe a DPA. 14:14:12 - Aisha Patel: we'll send SOC2, network diagram, DPA template. recommend security contact to coordinate. 14:14:35 - Liam Chen: quick note on observability: the Console integrates tracing hooks and you can export per-token traces for troubleshooting, but we redact sensitive tokens by default. 14:14:55 - Dana Ortiz: nice. what about cost allocation to our internal teams? 14:15:10 - Liam Chen: tagging routes and automatic daily cost allocation is the standard. you can also route traffic via different tenant ids for isolation. 14:15:35 - Marcus Blythe: what about compliance for EU data residency? 14:15:45 - Sofia Ruiz: we have region controls in Private and Hosted with region pins; we can deploy to specific cloud regions to satisfy residency. 14:16:10 - Aisha Patel: ok let's look at an example export - CSV sample shows columns: date, route, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, tokens_total, cost_usd, tags. 14:16:45 - Tom Reynolds: we've got a procurement cycle Q4; if pilot goes well procurement will push for Dedicated next quarter. 14:17:05 - Dana Ortiz: one more question on Optimize, does it run continuously or on-demand? 14:17:18 - Liam Chen: Optimize runs analyses periodically and can also be triggered on-demand; recommendations are surfaced in Console and we can set auto-apply rules with guardrails. 14:17:45 - Aisha Patel: wrap up: we'll send pricing, SOC2 & network diagram, and a pilot runbook. can we aim to start the pilot week of Aug 10? 14:18:05 - Marcus Blythe: yes that works. 14:18:12 - Dana Ortiz: we'll send sample traffic by Aug 5. 14:18:20 - Aisha Patel: great thanks everyone! 14:18:28 - meeting ends
notes: Customer is cost-sensitive due to long completion tokens (healthcare summaries)
Recommend starting with hosted pilot to capture real token distribution, then evaluate Dedicated pricing
Security checklist requested: SOC2 report, DPA, network diagram, KMS integration details
